newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaican exports decline, trade gap high.
newsitem.headline: Jamaican exports decline, trade gap high.

text.p: Figures issued by the Statistical Institute of Jamaica (Statin) Friday showed a four percent decline in the nation's exports for the first six months of this year, including an 11 percent fall-off in garment export volumes.
As a result, Jamaica's trade gap hit a 10-year high of US$653.3 million as of June 30.
According to Statin, total exports stood at US$718.1 million, down four percent over 1995, while total imports rose 6.7 percent, to US$1.37 billion.
Consumer goods imports registered the largest increase, growing 17.6 percent to US$348.5 million over the period.

On the export side, all sectors declined except for manufactured goods, which recorded a 12 percent increase. Mining, which includes bauxite and alumina, fell six percent, with earnings of US$322.4 million.

The non-traditional export sector fell 6.1 percent - this includes the apparel sector, Jamaica's largest export earner after bauxite. Garment export volumes were down 11 percent for the first six months of this year, while earnings fell two percent, to US$246 million.

Peter King, chairman of the Kingston-based Caribbean Textile and Apparel Institute, said the figures proved that Mexico continued to draw business and investment away from the Caribbean, and the region must get the same duty treatment as Mexico under the North American Free Trade Agreement if the garment sector is to survive.

For the entire Caribbean, garment earnings rose three percent for the first six months, to US$2.56 billion, King noted, while Mexico's garment export volumes rose 38 percent and earnings increased 32 percent.
